poster.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)

brief.title: Bot Mitigation at Scale: How Modern Web Security Services Protect Scientific Publishing Platforms
brief.one_liner: An analysis of how challenge-based bot verification systems safeguard high-value academic web properties against automated threats.
brief.goal: The viewer should understand the scale of bot traffic threatening academic publishers, the mechanisms used by CDN-based security services to mitigate these threats, and the measurable impact on platform availability and integrity.

sections.title: The Bot Threat Landscape for Academic Publishers
sections.objective: Present the scale and nature of malicious bot traffic targeting scientific content platforms.

sections.title: Challenge-Based Verification Pipeline
sections.objective: Explain the multi-stage verification workflow from initial request interception to successful access grant.

sections.title: Performance and Security Outcomes
sections.objective: Show quantitative results of deploying CDN-level bot mitigation on a major science publisher.

sections.title: Usability vs. Security Trade-offs
sections.objective: Discuss the balance between blocking bots and maintaining seamless access for legitimate researchers.
